text:
maria: Quick sync — we need a compact per-route KPI card in Console that shows p50/p95/p99 token latency, throughput, and error rate but also lets us slice by kernel selection, batching mode, and KV cache hit/miss. Current dashboard is too coarse.

sam: +1. main pain: noisy spikes from long-tail token latency that only show up in p99. ops can’t triage which kernel/batch combo caused it.

kevin: are we planning to store token-level latencies raw? that’ll explode cardinality. we might need sampling + histograms.

anya: we should do stratified sampling: full traces for 1/1000 requests, and histogram buckets for all routes. t-digest or HDR histogram for pXX.

lena: for Console UX, card needs dropdowns for: route, model variant, kernel (fused/naive/quant), batching_policy (adaptive/fixed), and kv_cache (hit/miss/all).

maria: agreed. proposal: emit two telemetry streams from runtime: 1) aggregate histograms per route+kernel+batching policy (low-cardinality keys) 2) sampled raw token latencies + metadata for debugging. histograms give p50/p95/p99 cheaply.

sam: example metrics schema: 
```
route.kv.histogram{route="/chat", kernel="fused", batching="adaptive", kv_hit="true"} -> HDR
route.tokens.sample -> [latency_ms, token_idx, kernel, batch_size, kv_hit, trace_id]
```

kevin: hdr okay, but ensure buckets align with Console bucketization. Also need percentiles to be computed server-side to avoid client slowness.

anya: for sampling, capture last-token latency + kv_hit boolean. those are the most indicative of tail. we can keep context length, model, and kernel. max sample rate 1/500 by default.

lena: UX question — how do we show p50/p95/p99 alongside throughput and error rate without overwhelming? my idea: compact card with three sparklines (latency p50/p95/p99), a throughput number (rps), and error %; expand to detailed view for breakdown by kernel/batch/kv.

maria: sounds good. also we need a token-waterfall drilldown page that stacks token-generation latency (kv lookup, kv io, attention kernel, token decode, network). each should be instrumented in runtime and exposed as sub-buckets so pXX sums make sense.

sam: runtime already tags stages: kv_lookup_ms, kernel_compute_ms, io_ms, decode_ms. we can emit histogram per stage with same aggregation keys. then Console can show stacked percentiles or median stack.

kevin: caution: some kernels have non-additive micro-op timing due to overlap (async copies). we should include a note: stage timings are approximations and may double-count overlap. still useful for triage.

maria: perf regression detection: want automated regression alerts when p95 for any route+kernel+batching combo increases >20% week-over-week or absolute p95 crosses SLO. We need baseline windows and burn-in smoothing.

anya: add signal for kv-miss spikes — a route with sudden kv_miss rate increase often correlates with p99 spikes. include kv_miss_rate metric.

lena: on retention + cost: full histograms per minute for all combos is heavy. limit full histograms to top N routes by traffic (configurable) and keep sampled histograms for others. older histograms can be downsampled (30d->daily rollup).

sam: implementation detail: in backend we can rollup per-minute HDR into hourly summaries using t-digest merge. that keeps percentiles accurate-ish.

kevin: kernel attribution: add dimension kernel_version and batch_size_bucket (1,2,3-8,9+). cardinality can explode; predefine batch_size buckets.

maria: action items: 1) eng-runtime: add histogram and sampled event emitters (kevin, sam) 2) eng-platform/Console: design card + expanded drilldown (lena, anya) 3) backend: storage retention + rollup plan (maria + ops)

kevin: I'll prototype metric tags and t-digest encoder this week. question: include trace_id in sampled events? yes for linking to profiler.

anya: profiler link should open a flamegraph with kernel timeline + batch boundary markers. we need consistent trace IDs between runtime traces and sampled token events.

lena: I'll mock the UI and a couple of sample queries for the backend. suggest Console exposes toggles: sample rate override, top-N route filter, and compare-to-baseline button.

maria: for alerts, default SLOs: p95 < 200ms (small models), p95 < 500ms (long-seq/large models), error_rate < 0.5%. can tune per-customer.

sam: last thought: add lightweight client-side header to requests with `x-routing-hint` to ensure routing info shows up in telemetry when we fallback to compatible model variants.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-metrics-proto branch -> staging at 1795000280 :rocket:

kevin: noted deploy. I'll attach a draft of the emitter PR to the ticket.

maria: thanks all. I'll create a tracking ticket in Jira with the three workstreams and link UX mockups. can we sync Monday for final scoping?

lena: monday works. :+1:

anya: i'll prepare example alert rules and SLO test harness.

sam: i'll run a quick cost estimate for histogram storage and sampling.

maria: perfect. closing thread for now, will reopen with the ticket link. :wave:
